description:
Project: Perf baseline & representative workload suite (Serving Runtime Performance: Kernel + Scheduling). Goal is to establish a locked, reproducible set of Q1 2026 latency/throughput baselines for Redwood’s top-served models across representative traffic shapes (prompt-length distributions, streaming vs non-streaming, concurrency, mixed tenants, batching pressure, cache hit rates). The baselines will become the reference for (1) runtime release qualification, (2) perf regression detection/gating, (3) model catalog performance profiles, and (4) customer-facing performance transparency (where approved).

Scope includes: defining the workload suite (synthetic + sanitized/aggregated “realistic” shapes), standardizing measurement methodology (TTFT, TPOT, end-to-end latency, throughput, error rates; p50/p95/p99; warm/cold cache), building/maintaining a benchmark harness and runner, integrating results into dashboards/alerts, and creating operational runbooks for reruns, variance investigation, and fleet/hardware normalization. In-scope components: runtime scheduler (prefill/decode scheduling, queueing/backpressure, load-shedding), kernel selection hot paths, KV cache behavior, batching policy interactions, telemetry correctness for perf metrics, and CI/nightly perf automation.

Key stakeholders: Runtime org (Mateo Alvarez; kernel team Hiro Tanaka; scheduling team Sofia Ivanova; Noah Patel/Grace Kim/Omar El‑Sayed/Lena Fischer/Marcus Reed/Yuki Sato), Applied ML perf/evals (Jonas Weber, Claire Dubois, Arjun Desai, Sana Farid) for methodology and model coverage, SRE/Observability (Sean Gallagher, Allison Grant, Aisha Bello, Sergio Costa) for variance + gating, Telemetry/Analytics (Logan Wright, Nadia Rahman, Caleb Johnson) for metric pipelines, Release Engineering (Connor O’Brien, Sahana Iyer) for release qualification, and Product (Henry Cho, Paula Mendes) for what gets published and how.

Timeline (Q1 2026):
- Weeks 1–2: agree on model list, hardware/regions, measurement definitions, and traffic-shape taxonomy; draft workload suite spec.
- Weeks 3–5: implement harness + runners; add instrumentation; stand up dashboards; validate repeatability and variance budgets.
- Weeks 6–8: execute baseline runs; triage anomalies; lock baseline artifacts (versioned configs, seeds, environment pins).
- Weeks 9–12: integrate regression gates into perf-canary + CI; define rollback criteria; publish internal docs and enable release qualification.

Constraints/risks: GPU fleet variance, multi-region noise, kernel autotuning nondeterminism, cache warmup effects, metric cardinality/cost, and confidentiality around any customer-derived workload signals. Deliverables include: Confluence “source of truth” docs + ADRs, a versioned workload suite in code, nightly/weekly benchmark pipelines with dashboards, and an explicit regression policy tied to runtime releases.

files.description: Published overview page: objectives, definitions (TTFT/TPOT/etc.), baseline philosophy, model/hardware/region matrix, and how teams should consume the baseline (release qualification + regressions).

Doc defining the canonical traffic shapes (prompt length distributions, output lengths, streaming/non-streaming, concurrency regimes, cache-hit scenarios), with rationale and mapping to common customer patterns.
Measurement methodology: run structure, warmup/cooldown, number of trials, statistical treatment, acceptable variance ranges, and how to compare across hardware SKUs.
Required runtime scheduler metrics (queue depth, batch composition, prefill/decode utilization, token counters, backpressure events) and how they’re used to explain p95/p99 behavior.
Company standard: what constitutes a regression vs noise, threshold rules by metric, exception process, and the required sign-offs for shipping runtime changes that move baselines.
How perf baselines map to SLO monitoring: which production SLOs should track which baseline metrics; guidance on alert thresholds and error-budget interpretation.
Specification for Grafana/Console dashboards: required panels, dimensions (model/region/hardware/traffic shape), drilldowns, and links to runs/commit SHAs.
Step-by-step playbook for investigating baseline deviations (kernel vs scheduler vs telemetry vs fleet), including profiler commands and common failure modes.
ADR covering how baseline artifacts are versioned (configs, prompts, seeds, runtime build, driver/CUDA versions), plus retention policy and reproducibility guarantees.
ADR deciding where the workload suite lives (repo ownership, review process, release tags), and rules for adding/removing workloads.
Post-rollout retrospective: what went well/poorly in baseline execution + gating rollout, action items for next quarter.
Internal release-note style announcement explaining the new baseline suite, where to find results, and what changes for runtime PRs/releases.
Working notes from kickoff (attendees, open questions, initial model list, proposed traffic shapes, action items). Less polished than Confluence.
Spreadsheet-style doc: model variants, context lengths, quantization profiles, and which hardware/regions each should run on; includes ownership and run priority.
Draft workload suite definition with example prompts, target token distributions, and notes on what’s synthetic vs derived from aggregated production signals.
First baseline run results table with p50/p95/p99, TTFT/TPOT, throughput, and variance annotations; links to dashboards and git SHAs.
SRE working doc for operating nightly baseline jobs: failure modes, paging criteria, and how to rerun safely.
Notes validating that telemetry for TTFT/TPOT matches ground truth; includes sampling strategy and known gaps.
Kernel microbench sweeps (sequence length, batch size, kv cache) to explain macro benchmark movements; used by kernels team to debug deltas.
Slide deck for release train: phases to introduce perf gates (warn-only → soft fail → hard fail), owners, and rollback plan.
Parent initiative ticket: “Perf baseline & representative workload suite (Q1 2026)” including goals, non-goals, milestones, and cross-team dependencies.
Define traffic-shape taxonomy and finalize the workload list (streaming, long-context, bursty concurrency, mixed prompt lengths); acceptance criteria includes sign-off from Runtime + SRE + Evals.
Implement workload suite versioning + artifact lock (configs, seeds, prompt sets) and define a baseline tag/release process.
Add scheduler instrumentation required for baseline explainability (batch composition, queue wait, backpressure counters) for the workload suite baselines.
Build benchmark runner for multi-region execution with environment pinning (driver/CUDA/runtime build) and standardized output schema.
Variance study: determine required run counts and confidence intervals per traffic shape; define ‘variance budget’ thresholds.
Integrate baseline runs into perf-canary with a nightly schedule; emit artifacts to dashboards and store run metadata.
CI gate policy: add a warn-only perf check on runtime PRs for key microbenchmarks; document exception workflow.
Kernel selection stability work item: reduce autotune nondeterminism for baseline-critical kernels; includes rollback plan.
Baseline dashboard buildout: required Grafana panels + drilldowns; includes ownership handoff to Observability.
Run baseline 'Run 1' and publish results; track anomalies and open follow-ups; links to Drive sheet and Confluence page.
PM ticket: define what baseline performance metrics can be shared externally (customer-facing benchmark transparency), approval workflow, and messaging guidelines.
Add TTFT/TPOT telemetry validation harness: compare runtime timestamps vs client-measured timings; ensure no telemetry metric regressions.
Release qualification checklist update: require baseline suite run for runtime release candidates; integrate with release-engineering process.
Document and automate baseline reruns on fleet changes (driver/CUDA upgrades, new instance types) and define criteria for when baselines must be refreshed.
PR adding initial workload suite schema + runner CLI; includes config validation, output JSON format, and example workloads.
PR adding traffic-shape generators (prompt length distributions, concurrency ramps, cache warmup phase) and baseline artifact packaging.
PR wiring nightly baseline runs, storing artifacts, and posting summary diffs to Slack; includes retry logic and failure classification.
PR adding Grafana dashboard JSON + alert rules for baseline drift (warn-only) and linking to run metadata.
PR adding scheduler metrics needed for baseline explainability (queue wait histograms, batch composition counters, backpressure events).
PR improving determinism for kernel auto-selection (pinning, seed handling, reduced autotune jitter) to stabilize baseline comparisons.
PR adding a ‘perf smoke’ CI job for key microbenchmarks; initially non-blocking with structured artifacts for perf-canary ingestion.
PR fixing TTFT instrumentation edge case for streaming responses (first chunk timestamp) uncovered during telemetry validation.
PR implementing scheduler change to cap tail latency under bursty workloads (load-shedding hook + fairness tweak) motivated by baseline Run 1 anomalies.
PR adding baseline config loader and runtime build metadata stamping into benchmark outputs for reproducibility.
PR adjusting default batching heuristics under mixed prompt lengths; includes before/after baseline results and rollout notes.
PR refactoring KV cache compaction counters and adding per-request cache state annotations for baseline analysis.
Thread coordinating kickoff logistics, owners, and initial model/traffic-shape shortlist; includes links to Linear ENG-4821 and Drive kickoff notes.
Thread debating TTFT definition for streaming (server vs client clock) and how to handle first-token chunking; leads to telemetry validation task.
Thread on baseline variance: reports noisy p99 on one region; includes hypotheses (fleet mix, driver version drift) and next steps.
Thread setting paging policy for nightly perf jobs (what alerts, what’s noise) and who owns reruns; references SRE runbook draft.
Thread reviewing ADR approach for baseline artifact versioning; quick comments from Runtime + Release Eng.
Thread coordinating when perf gates become blocking in CI; includes Connor O’Brien and Sahana Iyer discussing rollout phases.
Thread clarifying required dashboard dimensions (model/region/hardware/traffic shape) and how to avoid metrics cardinality blowups.
Thread triaging baseline Run 1 anomaly: regression only for long-context streaming; includes logs snippets and links to redwood PRs.
Thread for a minor internal perf incident (nightly baseline job flagged a severe regression; later found to be fleet driver mismatch); includes mitigation steps.
Thread with Applied ML perf/evals weighing in on workload representativeness and statistical methodology; links to variance budget doc.
Support ticket: enterprise customer reports increased p95 latency for streaming chat after a runtime upgrade; investigation uses baseline suite to reproduce traffic shape.
Support ticket: dedicated customer sees throughput drop under bursty concurrency; mapped to scheduler fairness/batching behavior; links to an eng-runtime Slack thread.
Support ticket: inconsistent TTFT reporting between Console and client measurements; drives telemetry validation work and a runtime fix PR.
Internal ticket: benchmark fleet environment drift (driver/CUDA mismatch) causing noisy results; includes proposed enforcement and remediation steps.
Technical deep dive transcript with a prospect asking for reproducible performance numbers; Redwood attendees explain baseline methodology and planned Q1 2026 publishable metrics.
POC scoping transcript where customer shares traffic patterns (prompt length mix, concurrency); Redwood maps it to workload suite shapes and proposes a benchmarking plan.
Combined security/performance review transcript: customer asks about data handling for workload capture and how Redwood avoids storing sensitive prompts while building representative shapes.
Company record for a latency-sensitive fintech prospect evaluating Dedicated; notes include strict p99 requirements, representative workload details, and links to Fireflies tech deep dive.
Company record for a customer/prospect focused on streaming support-agent workloads; includes throughput targets and baseline-related next steps.
Company record for a devtools company comparing providers on long-context performance; CRM notes mention baseline suite and planned benchmark report.
Email thread: Ava Chen, Mateo Alvarez, Sean Gallagher align on making baselines a release requirement; includes asks for resourcing and a timeline checkpoint.
Email thread: Dedicated PM + leadership looped on an enterprise customer requesting benchmark attestation; discusses what can be shared and references PM-612.
Email thread: Release Engineering coordinating with Runtime + CI owners on when perf gates move from warn-only to blocking; includes proposed policy language.
